points.problem: Associate an async context with its existing task serial and initialize retirement state
points.evidence: Original WWS32WSAStartup initializes native Winsock process-wide once, while task startup uses existing WWS32ThreadSerialNumber. Original WWS32TaskCleanup removes TLS and frees per-task data;the global async list has no task owner. Original DispatchPostMessage invokes PostAsyncGetHost, which copies to context->vBuffer16 before PostMessage validates the target window. Thus a queued success surviving task cleanup can address a departed task buffer;socket cleanup cannot identify these database requests. Reusing the existing serial in each context allows the same list owner to retire only that task. malloc_w does not zero memory;the current retirement state must start at zero before provider submission/list insertion.
points.minimum: Keep these two assignments pending owner decision. Moving ownership to a second lookup table duplicates state. Zeroing the entire context with a different allocator adds a replaced original call without reducing the field contract. The complete rundown algorithm is reviewed separately at R1797;this does not approve all of it.
points.limits: Complete source-level lifetime counterexample, not a measured scheduling race. Necessity of task ownership does not prove all four current retirement bits minimal.
